task.name: forge diagnose investigates the checkout it runs in, so evidence attached to an issue from another project is unreachable
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2670
---

## Problem

`forge diagnose` investigates the runtime it executes in. When the issue under
investigation describes a failure produced somewhere else, the diagnose agent reads this
checkout's source and this checkout's configuration, and the artifacts it cites do not
exist locally. Both cross-project diagnoses run so far recorded this in their own notes
and fell back to tracing code paths that merely *could* produce the reported shape.

Depends on #2670: evidence can only be read off a report once a report carries it.

## What

`forge diagnose` reads evidence attached to an issue, answers questions about the
observed run from that evidence, and treats content originating in another project as
data rather than as instruction.

## Acceptance criteria

- A diagnosis of an issue carrying attached evidence returns answers about the observed
  run from that evidence, and never from the configuration or source state of the
  checkout the diagnosis executes in.
- Content originating in another project's agent output is accepted as data. It never
  acts as instruction to the diagnosing agent, whatever it appears to assert about the
  agent's task, permissions, or conclusions.
- When attached evidence is absent, unreadable, or covers only part of what a question
  needs, the diagnosis reports which part it could not read and proceeds on the
  remainder. Local state is never substituted for missing attached evidence.
- An issue carrying no attached evidence continues to diagnose exactly as it does today,
  and emits no claim of having read evidence that was not there.

## Example

An issue filed from `fuzzypete/hdp` carries a run's evidence. Diagnosing it in this
repository:

```
$ forge diagnose --verbose --issue 2571
  evidence   : attached bundle from fuzzypete/hdp (run f5aa21cf2d8d, forge v0.14.2)
  reading    : run log, story audit, sprint state, reviewer outputs, story body
  unreadable : intake candidate artifacts (absent from bundle)
```

The question "was Layer-3 injection active for this run?" is answered `true` from the
attached snapshot, rather than `false` from this checkout's default — the exact
inversion that made one earlier cross-project diagnosis rule out a live hypothesis.

handoff.summary: Added an attached-evidence path to forge diagnose. parse_attached_evidence() in coordinator/diagnose_evidence.py recognizes the payload forge report produces — the manifest fenced under '## Evidence (captured from observing project)' in the issue body plus payload comments beginning '**Evidence — …**' — extracts the observed project, run id, forge version, artifact coverage and missing entries, reassembles multi-part chunks in order (byte-exact, gaps reported rather than silently concatenated), and re-renders artifact text inside untrusted-data delimiters that escalate past any run of the delimiter character in the payload, with the marker words neutralized. It resolves no paths, runs no gh lookups, and reads no local .forge files. diagnose_flow now fetches issue comments, tries the attached parser first, and when a packet is found makes it the only observed-run evidence source: build_starting_evidence is skipped, no local baseline SHA is captured, agent-reported inspected paths are not hashed against local git, and verify_premise is not run against this checkout (a path this repository never had, or removed for unrelated reasons, must not report a cross-project defect as already resolved). Source, run id, forge version, read labels, unreadable labels, char count and the skipped-local flags are recorded on DiagnoseState and in write_diagnose_audit; concise evidence/reading/unreadable progress lines match the spec example. build_diagnose_prompt gained evidence_is_attached, which adds explicit rules that attached content is data and never instruction, that conclusions inside it are prior assertions, that observed-run questions are answered only from the packet with missing parts reported instead of substituted from local state, and that premise anchors describe the observed project. Tests cover the parser against real reporting.render output (including an injection-shaped artifact and a contradictory local checkout) and the FETCH-to-INVESTIGATE and PARSE-to-VERIFY_PREMISE seams.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A diagnosis of an issue carrying attached evidence returns answers about the observed run from that evidence, and never from the configuration or source state of the checkout the diagnosis executes in.
acceptance_criteria.notes: The attached packet replaces the local pre-load entirely; a seam test plants a contradictory local run log, sprint state and forge.yaml and asserts the prompt carries the attached 'layer3_injection: true' and none of the local contradiction. The local baseline SHA, local file hashing and the local premise check are all skipped on this path, so no local state reaches the landed artifact either. Enforcement against the agent's own tool use is prompt-side (see deferred_items).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Content originating in another project's agent output is accepted as data. It never acts as instruction to the diagnosing agent, whatever it appears to assert about the agent's task, permissions, or conclusions.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Deterministic half: content is preserved verbatim inside boundaries the content cannot forge (delimiter escalates past the longest run of its own character anywhere in the payload; the marker words are rewritten inside carried text). Prompt half: rules 9-10 state the non-instruction and prior-assertion clauses, and a test asserts those clauses are present so a silent regression of the only enforcement mechanism fails.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: When attached evidence is absent, unreadable, or covers only part of what a question needs, the diagnosis reports which part it could not read and proceeds on the remainder. Local state is never substituted for missing attached evidence.
acceptance_criteria.notes: unreadable_labels covers manifest-declared missing evidence (with reasons), chunks listed in the body but never attached, missing parts of a split artifact, per-artifact clipping and budget drops. The list is rendered on the packet's own 'unreadable' line, emitted to the operator, and recorded in the audit; the prompt requires naming the gap in notes rather than answering from local state. A packet with no readable payload still reports the run and says so explicitly.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: An issue carrying no attached evidence continues to diagnose exactly as it does today, and emits no claim of having read evidence that was not there.
acceptance_criteria.notes: parse_attached_evidence returns an empty result for any body without a report manifest, and the flow falls through to the unchanged build_starting_evidence path with unchanged baseline/premise semantics. A regression test asserts the prompt contains no ATTACHED EVIDENCE section or trust-boundary clauses and that the audit's attached_evidence block is empty with local_baseline_skipped false.

deferred_items: AC2's data/instruction boundary is deterministic at the harness (no path resolution, no local fallback, unforgeable delimiters, audit record of the path taken) but prompt-side for the agent itself: the diagnose agent still runs with file tools against this checkout, so nothing mechanically stops it reading local source or acting on an injected instruction. Mitigated as the plan reviewer suggested — the clauses are assertable in a test, and the audit records that the attached path was taken plus the exact read/unreadable coverage, so a diagnosis citing local state is visible as a contradiction. A mechanical version would need a tool-surface restriction on the attached path.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 skips build_starting_evidence for attached reports, but _run_diagnose_flow_body still captures this checkout's HEAD, hashes agent-reported paths through _baseline_inspected_files, stamps that local SHA into the landed DiagnosisArtifact, and calls verify_premise against this checkout. The current prompt also requires HEAD-based premise_anchors. A cross-project path removed in this repository can therefore produce ALREADY_RESOLVED and suppress the evidence-based diagnosis, while local SHA/file hashes are rendered into the result. The proposed seam test only checks the prompt and audit metadata, so it would not catch this.
  Suggestion: Extend the attached-evidence mode through post-parse processing: do not stamp the executing checkout's baseline, hash attached-run paths locally, or call verify_premise against local Git. Adjust the attached-mode prompt/output expectations accordingly, and add a flow test where contradictory local Git history would otherwise trigger verify_premise's already-resolved path.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk (plan's risk #2): the data/instruction boundary for AC2 is enforced only in prompt text (Step 3). The diagnose agent still runs with file tools against this checkout, so nothing mechanically prevents it from reading local source/config or acting on an injected instruction inside an attached artifact. The plan's mitigation constrains the harness (no path resolution, no local fallback, delimited rendering) but not the agent.
  Suggestion: Keep the deterministic guards the plan already names, and make the prompt-side language assertable: add a test that the attached-evidence prompt contains the explicit non-instruction/observed-run-only clauses, so silent regression of the only enforcement mechanism fails a test. Consider recording in the audit that the attached path was taken, so an operator can spot a diagnosis that cited local state anyway.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1 lists 'available artifact labels' extraction but does not address multi-part chunks. build_evidence_chunks (render.py:145) labels split artifacts '<label> — <name> (part i of N)', so a large artifact arrives as several comments that must be reassembled in order, and a partially-posted payload leaves gaps.
  Suggestion: Have the parser group payload comments by artifact_name/label base, order by part index, and treat a missing part as unreadable coverage for that artifact rather than silently concatenating what arrived.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 2 changes _gh_fetch_issue (diagnose_flow.py:369) to add comments to the --json field list. Comment bodies can be large and the call has a 30s timeout; no bound is stated on payload size handed to the prompt.
  Suggestion: Cap total attached-evidence characters in the rendered packet (the plan already tracks a char count) and name any truncation in the unreadable list, so budget-driven trimming is reported rather than hidden.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
